weeds.note: Weeds grow on every field patch every question, planted or not: ratePerQuestion × weed tier of the chapter × (1 + fertilizerFactor × fertilizer points the patch density needs) × weed multipliers (edging, borders, geese, goat, mulch…). Weeds do not slow growth; each whole weed on a patch takes a share of its harvest (see crowding) and lowers the grade. One weeding tap clears weedsPerPull weeds; each weed costs 1 energy (less with hoes) and gives 1 fiber. Orchard spots grow half as many. The first freeDensity plants per patch need no fertilizer; each plant beyond needs 1 fertilizer point per planting.
weeds.diminishing: Weeding has no floor: you can always 'Root out the weeds' (a polish) — the first time cuts regrowth most, every next time half as much and costs more energy, because the last weeds are harder to find.

water.note: Water never comes by itself: every drop is carried. A trip with the old bucket brings fetchBase 💧 for fetchEnergy ⚡ (gathering upgrades make it cheaper). Wells, the yoke, the dug-out pond and more make each trip bring more and the store hold more, so later on you carry water less often. Rain waters the fields: planting costs no water until the next question.

wetShade.note: How light the soil of a patch looks (1 = dry), by growth steps since it was watered (visible-work/04). A patch is watered when it is planted (the water is spent then), and every worked patch is while it rains; the soil then dries as the plants grow, in a straight line between these [steps, brightness] points, and stays at the last one. Only the picture changes: nothing is saved.

pests.note: Every question, pests arrive in proportion to the plants growing (ratePerPlant × plants × chapter tier × season × (1 − fence block)). The scarecrow (and cat, owl, ducks) chases up to 'scare' pests away per question and leaveRate of the rest wander off. The pests that stay eat a share of every growing patch: eatPerPest × pests (at most maxEat), worked out exactly every question and shown rounded to a whole percent; a patch never drops below 1 plant. All this happens once per question; the map plays it when the farm is seen again after the Time Quiz: the scarecrow throws as many angry looks at once as its level (1–4), then the pests that stayed come one by one, eat a plant and carry it off, and come back a few seconds later.

stones.note: In winter, frost lifts stones in every field patch (more in deep beds and bare beds). Stones do not slow growth; like weeds each whole stone takes a share of the patch's harvest (see crowding) and lowers the grade. Picking them gives stones for walls, paths and buildings.

crowding.note: Weeds and stones crowd a patch (rules 2026-10-30, crops-and-items/02): at harvest, every whole weed and every whole stone on the patch takes perThing (4 %) of the harvest, together at most max (75 %), and the main crop never drops below keepMain. What is lost is shown (the plants stand wilted and grey on the patch, and the lost crops fade away as grey ghosts at harvest). Pulling the weeds and picking the stones before the harvest gives it all back. Weeds and stones no longer slow growth. They also still lower the grade of the whole harvest (rules/47-quality.json).

seedSaving.note: Seed from your own plants (crops-and-items/01, U2). A crop with seedYear (carrot, onion, beet: they flower only in their second year) can be left to flower once the card named here is read: the chore let_flower. A ripe patch then stays in the ground through one whole winter (the winter that is half over does not count) and is ripe with seed in the first spring after; harvesting it gives seedYield (on the crop) seeds per plant. Grain is the seed already (seedItem) and needs none of this. Seeds can always be bought.

rotation.note: A patch remembers its last crop. The same crop again grows 15% slower (tired soil); after beans or clover the next crop grows 10% faster (rested soil).

yield.note: Crop yields are averages per plant. Each plant gives its average × (1 + luck × luckShift) × the patch's quality, plus a random spread (spread × average), rounded up or down at random so the average is kept. The first item of a crop is at least minMain per plant. Upgrades raise the average (yield_<item> adds to every harvest).

carry.note: Carrying gear (effect add.carry) makes a gathering tap take 1 + carry loads at once: outputs and energy both grow with it, so the energy per piece stays the same, but more comes in per question (each spot refills once per question). A tap takes a smaller load when energy is short.

spring.intro: Weeds sprout fast now, and the rain waters your fields. A good time to sow.

summer.intro: Crops grow fastest, but the soil is dry and more pests come. Carry plenty of water.

autumn.abundance: Fruit and nuts: orchard +40%; branches fall (sticks ×2).
autumn.intro: Crops grow a little slower and the weeds slow down. Sow winter wheat now: it sleeps under the frost and wakes in spring.

winter.intro: Crops grow at a quarter of their speed. Snow covers the empty patches: clear it before you sow. Outside only hardy crops can be sown: winter wheat, onions, beans and kale. The house needs firewood.
winter.abundance: Frost brings stones up (pick them for walls); indoor work by the fire −10% energy; wool grows thick.

seasons.note: Seasons only change speeds and amounts — nothing dies. Crops grow at a quarter of their speed in winter (the greenhouse doesn't care). The season shows how many questions are left until the next one.

freshness.rule: At each change of season, food that has already lived through shelfLife season changes turns stale: plant food becomes Feed Mash, eggs and dairy go to the Compost pile. A 'stale soon' badge shows on anything that will turn at the next change — sell it, eat it, or cook it into something that keeps.
freshness.note: Cellar Racks add 1 season to everything; the Cool Cellar card adds 1 more. Preserved goods never spoil: flour, honey, jam, pickles, aged cheese, oils, cider, vinegar, grains, seeds, nuts.

muck.note: Each collection leaves muck (hens 0.3, cows 1, sheep 0.6 per animal). Above thresholdPerAnimal × animals the animals give 25% less; above twice that, 50% less. Mucking out costs energyPerMuck per muck and gives manure (compost!).

fence.note: The fence round a pen (hens, cows, sheep; bees have none; animal nodes with fenced: true) has three stages: broken at the start (the pen gives `broken` of its yield, about 10% less), mended (the first upgrade, pen_fence_<animal>_1: normal), sturdy and painted (the second, _2, which replaces the first: 1 + sturdyBonus, about 5% more). The same numbers for every fenced pen. The stage is the node effect set fence:<animal node> (1 or 2; no upgrade = 0).

fuel.note: Heat stations take recipe.fuel points from the woodpile per batch (campfire 1, stove 1, oven 2, kiln 3, forge 2…). The home burns homeFuel per question in winter (tent 0.2 → farmhouse 0.4; the hearth −30%). Stack wood onto the woodpile any time; the woodpile holds woodpileCap points (basket 20, shed 40, warehouse 80).
